summary: The stale verdict mattered: the uat merge had broken three of this slice's rows. SL-074 (9e99d00), merged into slice/SL-075 as 77ed010, deleted the '# settled by SL-043' block from .taad/fitness.yaml. F20, F21 and F23 named those settled rules in `also_settled`. `harness.py --scenario all` on the merged tree measured 52 rows, 49 AS-RECORDED, 3 MISSED-BY-FITNESS, exit 1: the missing hits were exactly the three deleted rules, with 0 stray hits. I removed those three names from `also_settled`. F23 keeps SL-044's 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore before the scan ends'. I also rewrote the one `_note` sentence that described them. After that, the recording run on the merged tree gives 52 rows, 52 AS-RECORDED, 0 stray hits, exit 0, and a clean baseline of 11 Facts and 61 rules with 0 hits. RuleCases -Case All holds everything, exit 0, and rules-parity is AGREE 11 <- 15, 27 patterns; 46 settled.

follow_ups: RuleCases.ps1 C-008 exercises only F01-F16 ($MustFire = 1..16). F17-F23 are measured only by a plain harness --scenario plants/all run. This lap shows why that matters: a yaml change in another slice (SL-074) broke three rows, and only a full harness run caught it, not `dotnet test` or RuleCases. Deriving $MustFire from the F-rows in plants.json would put them under RuleCases.

When a slice deletes or renames a settled fitness entry, nothing flags the plants.json `also_settled` rows that name it until someone runs the harness with the engine. A cheap check that every `also_settled` name is a rule in fitness.yaml (in rules-parity or in the harness's load_rows) would catch that at edit time.
